content.title: Gauff pulls away late to defeat rising Sun in Beijing
content.description: Coco Gauff won nine of the final 10 games to earn a 7-5, 6-1 victory over 16-year-old Sun Xinran on Monday and reach the Beijing Round of 16 for the fourth straight year. The win improved Gauff to 24-4 in her career against younger opponents.

content.body:
Coco Gauff has typically had her way against younger players, and that trend continued Monday night in Beijing, though not without a fight. The World No. 4 pulled away late, winning nine of the final 10 games to beat 16-year-old Sun Xinran 7-5, 6-1 in 1 hour, 29 minutes and advance to the Round of 16 for the fourth consecutive year.

Beijing: Scores | Order of play | Draws

Gauff has now won 24 of her 28 career matches at the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz level against opponents younger. Her only loss to a teenager during that span came against eventual champion Victoria Mboko in Montreal in 2025.

Returning to the Round of 16 💪 @CocoGauff moves past Sun in straight sets and continues to push towards a place at WTA Finals Indian Wells! #ChinaOpen https://t.co/Ksy9n9xbLI

— wta (@WTA) October 5, 2026

Despite the result, Gauff had nothing but praise for the young Chinese standout.

"I think she's a little bit more mature than I was at 16," Gauff said in her post-match interview. "I think I got a little bit more frustrated than she did. But she's an incredible player. I knew going in it was going to be a tough match. The junior career that she's had is incredible, and obviously she's going to do great at this level.

"I think this is the first of many matches on this court and many matches that we will play against each other. I'm looking forward to the future matchups we have."

More to come...

content.title: Zheng holds off Bouzkova in third straight three-setter in Beijing
content.description: Zheng Qinwen narrowly defeated Czechia's Marie Bouzkova in 2 hours and 54 minutes in her third straight three-setter in Beijing. She will next face Alina Charaeva in the Round of 16.

related.label: Swiatek rallies from 6-4, 5-2 down to beat Vekic and reach Beijing last 16
Around Beijing: Ostapenko enters influencer era as Sakkari's mindset evolves
Potapova shuts down 2026 season after Beijing retirement

content.body:
BEIJING -- Three matches in, and it's another three-setter for Zheng Qinwen. 

In a close 7-6(3), 4-6, 7-5 win over No. 18 seed Marie Bouzkova in 2 hours and 54 minutes, Zheng is through to the Round of 16 at the China Open for the first time since 2024 after her third consecutive match that went to a decider.

"I just think I believe here everybody wants to take me down," Zheng said to press. "They really show up [with] their best tennis. I believe somehow they prove that the level was really high."

She will next face Alina Charaeva, who is in the middle of an unexpected run to the fourth round after defeating Sonay Kartal Monday just days following her upset win over World No. 1 Elena Rybakina. 

Zheng, a wild card in Beijing, has now played a total of eight hours and one minute on court, the most of any player thus far the China Open, but has grinded out the win when it matters most in the deciding set. Of her 21 wins this season on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz, Zheng has won 13 of them in deciding sets. 

During her post-match press conference, Zheng quickly pointed to a moment when she led 3-1 in the first set that in hindsight she wished she did better mentally. On Bouzkova's serve, Zheng created a triple break opportunity, but Bouzkova ultimately held. 

MATCH FOR THE AGES ⭐️ Zheng Qinwen moves into the Round of 16 in Beijing defeating Bouzkova in a three-set thriller that we couldn’t take our eyes off! #ChinaOpen https://t.co/VR1tqKHXIv

— wta (@WTA) October 5, 2026

Before the tournament, Zheng explained how Beijing feels like her fifth Grand Slam, and that she truly wants to put on a strong outing for her home-crowd. While the Chinese crowd gives her plenty of motivation, she's trying to let the pressure build like it did in that early moment in the first set.

"Of course, I'm really happy to win because I felt like maybe [the opponent] plays without pressure, but I felt I really play with lot of pressure because I want to perform well in front of my home crowd," Zheng said. "This gives me energy, but in the same time I believe maybe I should be a bit more chill, more relax on court, especially when I'm leading 3-1 in the first set.

"Those mistakes... I believe I should [have] done it better."

Throughout the match, Zheng put pressure on Bouzkova's serve, forcing 12 break-point chances and winning 36% of Bouzkova's first-service points and 53% of her second-service points. On Zheng's serve, her 81% success rate on first-service points (46-of-57) and 11 aces might have just been the difference -- her 26 aces this tournament are the most of any player. 

Zheng said she didn't put too much of en emphasis on her serve during practice ahead of the tournament, and though she wants to see stronger results, it's been one of her biggest weapons in Beijing and she's more pleased with how she's developed the points. 

"There was some ups and downs in my practice, I thought I could have done better," Zheng said. "What makes me happy is what I did after my serve. I didn't really practice previously, but I did better in the matches. This is something I should celebrate."

Zheng has a strong opportunity to advance to the quarterfinals against Beijing debutant Charaeva, and Zheng holds a 1-0 advantage in the head-to-head -- a 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 win in Marbella, Spain six years ago. She's seen bits and pieces of Charaeva's matches, but isn't too familiar with her game and didn't recall the match in 2020.

"To be honest, I might have seen her matches, but a little bit [of an] impression of her game, not so much. [I'm] not very familiar. After this press conference I will do my homework."
content.summary: Zheng Qinwen narrowly defeated Czechia's Marie Bouzkova in 2 hours and 54 minutes in her third straight three-setter in Beijing. She will next face Alina Charaeva in the Round of 16.

content.title: Swiatek rallies from 6-4, 5-2 down to beat Vekic and reach Beijing last 16
content.description: Iga Swiatek erased a 6-4, 5-2 deficit against Donna Vekic to extend her perfect record against the Croatian and reach the China Open round of 16. The former champion won the second-set tiebreak 7-0 before completing a 4-6, 7-6(0), 6-2 comeback in 2 hours, 40 minutes.

related.label: By the numbers: Bartunkova stuns Sabalenka to reach Beijing last 16
Osaka delivers in key moments to outlast Bejlek in Beijing third round
Rybakina withdraws from Wuhan after early China Open exit

content.body:
Iga Swiatek had won all four of her previous meetings with Donna Vekic, dropping just one set. But in their China Open third-round match Monday in Beijing, No. 30 seed Vekic appeared poised to end that run after taking a 6-4, 5-2 lead.

Swiatek, the 2023 champion, refused to let the match slip away. She broke Vekic twice to level the second set at 5-5, then won the tiebreak without losing a point to force a decider.

After the players exchanged breaks to open the third set, Swiatek broke again for a 3-2 lead and closed out a 4-6, 7-6 (0), 6-2 victory in 2 hours, 40 minutes.

"For sure I was in a bad position score-wise, didn't really know after the first set what to change to play better," Swiatek told the media after the win. "Later on in the second set I was playing more brave and more aggressive, changing more down the line. At the end I think it's what changed the rhythm of the match.

"I don't know how many points we both had, but I felt like I'm playing good. I felt like we might be even, but maybe she was winning the more important points. I knew I had my opportunities; I should push a little bit more. I just needed to go level up because she played really good, used these chances that I didn't use in the first set."

Comeback complete ✅ Iga Swiatek storms back to defeat Vekic in a three-set thriller! #ChinaOpen https://t.co/l7wTbYuaWF

— wta (@WTA) October 5, 2026

For Vekic, the loss marked her third defeat to a top-10 player in 2026, having previously lost to Mirra Andreeva at the Australian Open and Jessica Pegula at Indian Wells.

Swiatek is through to the round of 16 at a WTA 1000 event for the 40th time in her career and will be bidding to win her 13th title at this level.

It was also Swiatek's 147th win at WTA 1000 events. Only Serena Williams, with 148, and Aryna Sabalenka, with 156, have more.

She moves on to face No. 10 seed Iva Jovic next. The American defeated Kamilla Rakhimova 6-1, 7-5 in another third-round battle on Monday.
content.author: WTA Staff
content.summary: Iga Swiatek erased a 6-4, 5-2 deficit against Donna Vekic to extend her perfect record against the Croatian and reach the China Open round of 16. The former champion won the second-set tiebreak 7-0 before completing a 4-6, 7-6(0), 6-2 comeback in 2 hours, 40 minutes.

leadMedia.title: From a set and a break down, Swiatek rallies to beat Vekic in Beijing third round

content.title: What's it like being a ball kid at the China Open? Here's what they said
content.description: At this year's China Open, there are 236 ball kids that get to share the court with some of the tournament's biggest stars. Here's a glimpse into the life of a China Open ball kid.

related.label: Swiatek rallies from 6-4, 5-2 down to beat Vekic and reach Beijing last 16
Potapova shuts down 2026 season after Beijing retirement
Osaka delivers in key moments to outlast Bejlek in Beijing third round

content.body:
BEIJING -- The China Open’s ball-kid program begins well before the first ball is struck, with 250 young candidates selected through trials beginning in August before the final group is chosen after an evaluation period.

This year, that group includes 236 ball kids -- 228 from China, four from Australia through a partnership with Tennis Australia and four from France through a collaboration with Roland Garros.

"Everyday is filled with joy when they're on court. They're happy, we try to make them healthy and we try to make them enjoy the time spent in China," Chloe Rong, Senior Manager of Competition Services, said. "That's our most important job, and [as long as] they're having fun, that's our job."

Some of the tournament's top ball kids were made available to the media, and here's what they had to say:

Zhang Xinyue, 16

Zhang, of China, found out about the possibility of being a China Open ball kid online through WeChat, and she applied instantly.

She brings Grand Slam experience to this year's Beijing group, serving as a ball kid at Roland Garros in 2025, where she was grateful to make many friends. Part of the partnership with Roland Garros is that the China Open will send its top ball kids to Paris. 

"I think it's very exciting for me," Zhang said. "It's a really good memory and experience to meet people and friends all over the world and experience famous and great players in tennis."

Zhang's favorite player is Zheng Qinwen, who is into the fourth round in Beijing. She's been following Zheng's journey after her elbow injury and recovery through the 2026 season on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz, where the highlight was reaching the quarterfinals at the US Open out of qualifying. 

"One of my favorite Chinese players is Zheng Qinwen," Zhang said. "I'm really glad to see her come back to the court again after her injury for quite a long time. I think it's really good for her to come back to China open and perform great on the quarter."

Talon Mackenzie, 16

Mackenzie, of Australia, attended the Australian Open in Melbourne back in 2022 and instantly knew he wanted to be a ball kid. 

So, he applied for the 2023 tournament, but then did not advance through the first round of qualifications. After skipping a year, he got accepted for the 2025 Australian Open and finished that tournament working the men's singles final. 

As a result of his strong reputation, Tennis Australia selected Mackenzie and three others to work the China Open. The China Open will similar send their top ball kids to Melbourne in addition to Paris and vice versa through a similar partnership. In Beijing, the Australian and French ball kids have a badge of their flag on the side of their cap. 

"I love tennis," Mackenzie said. "It's so awesome to just be on court with these players. It's the best seat in the house. I just tell my friends that there's no better way to spend January. It's to go to the AO."

One of the highlights was being a ball kid during on of Coco Gauff's matches at this year Australian Open during her run to the semifinal, and in Beijing, he had to chance to be on court with one of his favorite players, Alex de Minaur.  

"It's so cool to see your idols playing on court," Mackenzie said. "You're so close to them, and you can hear their conversations and get an understanding of how they're playing and how they're thinking. It's such a completely different experience compared to being in the stands."

In Beijing, Mackenzie has also had the time to explore, going on a trip to the Great Wall of China and visiting Universal Studios with other ball kids.

On-site, he's enjoyed the thrilling atmosphere of the crowd and being on court during some of the entertaining matches with players the Chinese fans rally behind.  

"China definitely does not disappoint for us, especially after a massive point and the crowd's going crazy," Mackenzie said. "All of us ball kids are doing our own thing under these pressure points, and the adrenaline rush is so crazy and so exciting."

Mackenzie has aged out of the Australian Open, so Beijing presents him the opportunity to bookend his ball kid career. 

"To have one more opportunity to come out and be with the players again is really exciting, and I'm really grateful to be able to do this again," Mackenzie said.

Li Xiaoyi, 15

Li has been a ball kid for the past four years at the China Open, and feels that the tournament has improved every year. He also went to Melbourne for his first Grand Slam as part of the Tennis Australia partnership.

From both tournaments, Li has seen the subtle differences in how each event operates in terms of procedures and standards. He also has come to appreciate the exchange in cultures of the program.

" China definitely does not disappoint for us, especially after a massive point and the crowd's going crazy. All of us ball kids are doing our own thing under these pressure points, and the adrenaline rush is so crazy and so exciting. "
Talon Mackenzie -- Ball kid at the 2026 China Open

"I think there are definitely differences in technique," Li said in Mandarin. "It's a process of mutual help and mutual improvement. We can also make friends and chat with them, which I think is pretty good."

Li's favorite part of the job is seeing five-star points on court-level, and then tossing the ball to the serving player at his request. Overall, every time he gets the 45 minutes per assignment to be on court, he soaks it all in. 

"When I see those kinds of nice key shots, I also feel happy," Li said. Including when they ask me for the ball, I also get very excited. Every time I serve [as a ball kid] them, I get very excited."

Joshua Yapi, 16

Yapi is one of four representing France, and back in May and June, he served as a ball kid at Roland Garros. That was a requirement to come to Beijing, and due to his high performance, he was selected to come to China. 

It's his first time in Beijing, and he's thorough enjoying his time at the tournament. 

"I think it's a very good organization, and the complex is super big,," Yapi said in French. "I feel comfortable here, we are well supported, we have a lot of support, the supervisors are very cool with us and the other participants help us a lot, so frankly I feel very good about the [opportunity]."

Yapi gave a glimpse into the pre-match training the group undergoes ahead of their daily schedules.

They'll conduct a short warm-up before practicing their rolls from center court to the baseline and vice versa to ensure the process is smooth without any disruption.

"Off the field, we try to work on our roll technique so that everything is perfect," Yapi said. "Our rolls have to be flat, fast, and precise."

content.title: Potapova shuts down 2026 season after Beijing retirement
content.description: Anastasia Potapova has decided to cut her 2026 season short to focus on getting fully healthy for 2027. While she produced strong results in throughout the season, it wasn't a completely healthy year for the Austrian.

related.label: Osaka delivers in key moments to outlast Bejlek in Beijing third round
By the numbers: Bartunkova stuns Sabalenka to reach Beijing last 16
Noskova, Andreeva stay in control, dodge Beijing upsets

content.body:
World No. 25 Anastasia Potapova has ended her 2026 season, she announced on social media. The decision comes a few days after Potapova retired in her opening match in Beijing against Sinja Kraus with a right shoulder injury. 

"My season has to come to an end," Potapova wrote. "Unfortunately, lately my body has been giving me more and more signs that it's time to stop. For me, that's the clearest sign that I need to take a break, give my body the times it needs to recover and come back stronger.

"See you in 2027!"

In 2026, Potapova had one of her best seasons on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz, improving her ranking from No. 97 ahead of Linz to a season-high and current No. 25. Her clay season was among the best of any player on tour, advancing the final in Linz, the semifinals in Madrid as a lucky loser, and the fourth rounds at Rome and Roland Garros. The highlight of her season was a 4-6, 7-6(1), 6-4 win over then-defending champion Coco Gauff at the French Open third round. 

Still, it wasn't a fully healthy season for the Austrian. At the beginning of the year in Australia, she was playing with a broken finger on her non-dominant hand. After Roland Garros, she retired in her second-round match at s'Hertogenbosch vs. Zeynep Sonmez with an illness.

The next tournament in Berlin, she retired after losing the first set to Ekaterina Alexandrova in the first round with a neck injury. 

Then, at the US Open last month, amidst a three-set battle with Mirra Andreeva, Potapova fell while chasing an Andreeva forehand, injuring her left-knee and requiring a medical timeout. At the time, Potapova was serving to stay in the match down 5-3, and though she did return to play with significant taping, she was clearly hampered and Andreeva closed out the match as Potapova left in tears. 

After Beijing, she was only scheduled to play Wuhan, but will now shift her focus to getting fully healthy for 2027. Last season, she did not play any events after Beijing either.

content.title: Osaka delivers in key moments to outlast Bejlek in Beijing third round
content.description: Naomi Osaka weathered difficult conditions and a determined challenge from Sara Bejlek to earn a 7-6 (4), 6-4 victory and reach the fourth round in Beijing. Osaka converted her fifth match point and delivered in the clutch to secure the win.

related.label: By the numbers: Bartunkova stuns Sabalenka to reach Beijing last 16
Noskova, Andreeva stay in control, dodge Beijing upsets
Charaeva upsets new World No. 1 Rybakina in Beijing second round

content.body:
Naomi Osaka passed a stern test against No. 20 seed Sara Bejlek on Sunday, overcoming a determined challenge to earn a 7-6 (4), 6-4 victory and advance to the Round of 16 in Beijing for the fourth time. The former World No. 1 needed just over two hours and five match points to secure the win.

Beijing: Scores | Order of play | Draws

Osaka not only had to fend off Bejlek, but also battle difficult playing conditions that included strong winds and cold temperatures.

"I'm really happy with how I played," Osaka said in her post-match interview. "Obviously the conditions weren't amazing, but we both have to play in them, so I never try to complain [about] that. She's an incredible player, so it's nice to have pulled out a two-set victory against her."

Little separated the two players throughout the match. Bejlek held four set points in the opening set and generated nine break-point opportunities overall, but Osaka excelled in key moments to win their first career WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz meeting.

Relief 😅

A tight encounter goes the way of @naomiosaka!#ChinaOpen pic.twitter.com/4NoXlA1R2C

— wta (@WTA) October 4, 2026

Osaka also continued to prove herself as one of the tour's best front runners. She improved to 28-2 this season when winning the first set, with her only losses in those matches coming against the world's top two players: Aryna Sabalenka in Madrid and Elena Rybakina in Toronto.

Here were three keys to Osaka's third-round win:

Clutch factor

Osaka delivered in the match's biggest moments. After being broken late in the first set, she broke back as Bejlek served for the set. A few games later, while serving to force a tiebreak, Osaka saved four set points -- including one with a well-timed volley winner -- before taking four of the final five points in the tiebreak to claim the opening set after 64 minutes.

After Bejlek double-faulted to hand Osaka a break for a 4-2 lead in the second, the four-time Grand Slam champion again rose to the occasion, saving three break points with a trio of overheads to consolidate for a 5-2 advantage.

Then, after a shaky service game in which she double faulted on match point and was broken while serving for the match, Osaka regrouped. She outlasted Bejlek in a five-deuce game -- the third of the match -- to earn the decisive break and close out the victory.

Overhead mania

While Osaka is best known for her serve and powerful groundstrokes, she frequently moved forward against Bejlek. The tactic paid off, highlighted by a series of overhead winners.

She unveiled a surprise serve-and-volley early in the first set, finishing the point with one of several overhead winners before holding at love for 2-2. Later, she used a backhand volley winner to hold for 3-3.

Her most emphatic overhead came in the first-set tiebreak, when she hammered a winner to bring up the only set point she would need. The overhead also proved crucial late in the second set, helping Osaka fend off a barrage of break points to maintain control of the match.

First-serve prowess

Given her track record, it was no surprise that Osaka excelled behind her first serve despite facing nine break points.

Big serve 👊 @naomiosaka takes the opening set, 7-6(4)! #ChinaOpen https://t.co/Gc8Yr9oEax

— wta (@WTA) October 4, 2026

She landed 69% of her first serves and won 76.7% (46 of 60) of those points. That efficiency proved especially important given that she won just 37% of points behind her second serve.

Coming into the match, Osaka ranked fourth on tour in first-serve points won at 72.3%, trailing only Rybakina, Zheng Qinwen and Linda Noskova.

What's next

Osaka will face No. 7 seed Karolina Muchova next. Muchova owns a 4-3 edge in her career head-to-head against Osaka, including wins at Bad Homburg and Wimbledon this year.

"I played Muchova recently in the quarters at Wimbledon, which sucked for me, but was great for her," Osaka told reporters. "She's an amazing player. She's someone that you know is very dangerous no matter what. She could pretty much beat anybody. But I think from my end, no matter who I play I just have to focus on myself."

content.title: Rybakina withdraws from Wuhan after early China Open exit
content.description: World No. 1 Elena Rybakina pulled out of Wuhan a day after her second-round exit and upset loss to Alina Charaeva at the China Open.

related.label: Noskova, Andreeva stay in control, dodge Beijing upsets
By the numbers: Bartunkova stuns Sabalenka to reach Beijing last 16
Charaeva upsets new World No. 1 Rybakina in Beijing second round

content.body:
World No. 1 Elena Rybakina has pulled out of the upcoming Dongfeng Voyah Wuhan Open because of injury, the tournament announced on social media. 

The decision comes a day after Rybakina was upset by World No. 118 Alina Charaeva in three sets in the second round of the China Open in Beijing. Rybakina is next scheduled to compete at the Ningbo 500, where she is the defending champion. Last year in Wuhan, she reached the quarterfinals. 

"I'm very sorry to the fans who were looking forward to seeing me play," Rybakina said in the Instagram story. "I'll take some time to rest and recover. Thank you for your understanding and continued support. See you next year."

Over the past few months, Rybakina has been dealing with a lingering lower leg and foot injury that caused her to retire during the quarterfinals of Cincinnati against Iga Swiatek.

She managed to recover well enough for the US Open, where Rybakina won her third Grand Slam title, captured the World No. 1 ranking and became the first singles player to qualify for the WTA Finals at Indian Wells. 

Rybakina joins Amanda Anisimova, Madison Keys, Emma Navarro and Karolina Pliskova as pre-tournament withdrawals. The Wuhan Open is scheduled for October 12-18 and is the final WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz 1000 event of the season.
content.author: Cole Bambini
content.summary: World No. 1 Elena Rybakina pulled out of Wuhan a day after her second-round exit and upset loss to Alina Charaeva at the China Open.

content.title: Noskova, Andreeva stay in control, dodge Beijing upsets
content.description: Reigning Grand Slam champions Linda Noskova and Mirra Andreeva avoided the upset bug at the China Open, needing just over two hours combined to speed into the fourth round.

related.label: By the numbers: Bartunkova stuns Sabalenka to reach Beijing last 16
Charaeva upsets new World No. 1 Rybakina in Beijing second round
Gauff, Sun set for Beijing battle in junior's first-ever top 5 matchup

content.body:
The upset bug has hit the China Open in a big way this weekend, with No. 1 seed Elena Rybakina and No. 2 seed Aryna Sabalenka exiting the tournament within 24 hours of each other.

The two newest and youngest Grand Slam champions on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz have proved immune, though. No. 5 seed and last year's runner-up Linda Noskova needed just 55 minutes to dismiss Viktorija Golubic 6-2, 6-1 to return to the fourth round. She followed No. 4 seed Mirra Andreeva, who came from 4-2 down in the first set against Polina Kudermetova to wrap up a 6-4, 6-1 win in 68 minutes.

Tactically, Noskova and Andreeva couldn't have been more contrasting -- but what they had in common was a complete command of their respective game styles. Wimbledon champion Noskova dominated with front-foot, first-strike tennis, firing 31 winners in total past Golubic and never allowing the Swiss player to build points on her own terms.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

The foundation of Noskova's win was, once again, her serve -- a shot that's becoming one of the most formidable weapons on tour. She landed 77% of her first serves, and conceded only five points behind it -- all in the second set. She suffered only one blip on serve, going down triple break point in the first game of the second set with three cheap unforced errors -- but even that game turned into a showcase of her ability. Three unreturned serves and two winners later, Noskova had reeled off five straight points for the hold.

"It was a different match than the first one, especially with the conditions," Noskova said to press. "It was a lot colder and much more windy. Once the match started, I had gotten into my rhythm and didn't really notice it." 

The Czech player's creativity was also on show. The quality of Noskova's serve frequently means she has options on her plus-one shot, and she kept Golubic guessing by constantly mixing up her choices: a delicate drop shot here, taking it out of the air on a drive volley there, or simply a routine power groundstroke into the open court. In the second set, the 21-year-old began to flex her variety on return as well, at one point rushing the net to pull off an exquisite angled backhand volley winner.

By contrast, Andreeva often found herself on the back foot against the offensively-minded Kudermetova. The Roland Garros champion only struck three winners off the ground -- six aces took her total to nine -- compared to Kudermetova's 25 (plus two aces). The No. 104-ranked Uzbek's best points showcased all-court ability as well as baseline power -- while her backhand was her most reliable weapon, Kudermetova's highlights also included impressive touch on the drop shot and at net.

However, Andreeva was able to tighten up her game in blustery conditions, while still elevating it in key moments. From 4-2 down in the first set, the 19-year-old won 10 of the next 11 games, reducing her unforced error count from 12 in the first set to just six in the second. She also saved all five break points against her in the second set, finding a signature backhand winner down the line and two of her aces on three of those occasions.

Kudermetova proved increasingly unable to find winning shots with any consistency, racking up 48 unforced errors in total.

"I think today I felt more comfortable being more, like, a little bit further away from the baseline," explained Andreeva afterwards. "Defending a lot, putting a lot of balls back in the court. I think that's what I've been doing not bad. I feel like that's also what she had trouble with. I knew no matter what I would just have to run for every ball and put as many balls back in the court as I can. I don't know, however I want to put them, slice, I don't know, drop shots. Whatever worked. That's kind of the tactics that I had for today."

Noskova will next face No. 19 seed Ekaterina Alexandrova, who came from a set and 2-0 down to defeat No. 11 seed Diana Shnaider 3-6, 6-4, 6-3 -- her third win in four meetings with the Roland Garros semifinalist. An unusual shot selection enabled Alexandrova to turn the match in her favor: down 2-1 in the second set, she broke up a big-hitting baseline battle with a casually flicked angled slice winner out of nowhere. It took Shnaider completely by surprise, and Alexandrova went on to capture the key break back in that game.

The 31-year-old advanced to the last 16 at WTA 1000 level or above for the second time in 2026 (following Cincinnati), and for the first time in her career in Beijing. Her record against Noskova is tied at 1-1 -- Alexandrova won their only hard-court encounter 7-6(5), 4-6, 6-2 in the 2025 Monterrey quarterfinals, but Noskova avenged that loss 6-1, 6-1 on the clay of Stuttgart this year.

Andreeva will face the surging Daria Snigur for the first time in the last 16. The Ukrainian needed just 47 minutes to rout Taylah Preston 6-1, 6-0, conceding just eight points in the second set to advance to the fourth round at a WTA 1000 tournament for the first time. It was a stark contrast to the World No. 46's first two matches in Beijing, in which she had to battle back from a set down to defeat both qualifier Katarzyna Kawa and No. 14 seed Jasmine Paolini.
content.author: WTA Staff
content.summary: Reigning Grand Slam champions Linda Noskova and Mirra Andreeva avoided the upset bug at the China Open, needing just over two hours combined to speed into the fourth round.

content.title: Around Beijing: Alexandrova returns to China Open last 16 as Andreeva returns to chess

related.label: By the numbers: Bartunkova stuns Sabalenka to reach Beijing last 16
Charaeva upsets new World No. 1 Rybakina in Beijing second round
Gauff, Sun set for Beijing battle in junior's first-ever top 5 matchup

content.body:
BEIJING -- Mirra Andreeva is now an avid chess player. 

The Roland Garros champion is a person of many hobbies, such as diamond painting, but the latest has been traditional board game. 

She used to learn chess when she was younger back in kindergarten, but as her tennis and education commitments racked up, chess was put to the side. 

Now, it's been revived in Andreeva's world, and her interest in chess was rekindled at Roland Garros, where the 19-year-old won her first Grand Slam title. Andreeva saw her fitness coach playing online just before each of her matches, and it sparked her interest.

"I just wanted to remember, wanted to learn again," Andreeva said after her 6-4, 6-1 win over Polina Kudermetova Sunday. "Starting, Roland Garros -- May and June -- that time I started playing chess again."

Since the tournament, she's been learning everyday on Duolingo to learn the tactical strategies. She also another app for matches against strangers, however you won't know that you're playing the six-time title winner on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz. 

"My nickname is very different. You would never guess what it is," Andreeva said. "It's going to stay a secret. If I tell, I'm going to be embarrassed if you know it."

Andreeva's not the lone -- current or active -- chess player on tour. Yulia Putintseva employed her aggressive tactics on the online game. Ekaterina Alexandrova, who is into the fourth round at the China Open, also learned to play chess earlier in her life with her father's instruction, but the game's forward-looking strategic thinking is something she needs to improve on. 

"For me, it's such a difficult game because you need to think three steps ahead, maybe five steps ahead and for me I'm always trying to survive the current situation without thinking so much," Alexandrova laughed. 

"It's super fun when you understand and you feel you have the smallest chances, but sometimes -- I know how everything [moves], but like it's not like the game. I mean, [it's] super difficult, but it can be fun."

JOB DONE ✅ No.4 seed Mirra Andreeva closes out the match against Kudermetova to move into the Round of 16 in Beijing. #ChinaOpen https://t.co/NqRT5y0so4

— wta (@WTA) October 4, 2026

Andreeva will face Daria Snigur and Alexandrova takes on Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova in the Round of 16 Tuesday. 

Alexandrova returns to Beijing win column 

Prior to Friday's second round, the last time Alexandrova had won in Beijing was seven years ago when she reached the Round of 16. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, she bowed out after just one match, but she's now back in the fourth round.

Her move into the final 16 comes after a three-set comeback win over Diana Shnaider. Alexandrova couldn't pinpoint the exact reason why things are clicking in Beijing this year, but she attributed that the change to the Yonex Tour Platinum ball fits her game. 

"The balls, they suit my game more than it used to be because the last couple of years I was quite unlucky here in Beijing, but hopefully this year, it's going so much better for me," Alexandrova said.

Generally, Alexandrova said she's appreciated the increase in uniformity of the balls from tournament to tournament over the season, and it's help the adjustment to the various court conditions of each stop on tour. 

"For sure, playing just a few consecutive tournaments with one, it just helps a lot because you can get used to that ball," Alexandrova added. "It's easier to to readjust and adapt to other tournaments because when you're switching every week, you need to adapt to the surface, to everything and to the balls.

"Sometimes, you don't have that much time. When we're playing more tournaments [with] one kind of ball, it helps so much more."

content.title: By the numbers: Bartunkova stuns Sabalenka to reach Beijing last 16
content.description: Nikola Bartunkova scored the biggest win of her career by defeating No. 2 seed Aryna Sabalenka in the third round of the China Open on Sunday. The Czech claimed her second career Top 10 victory and advanced to the round of 16 for the second time at a WTA 1000 event.

related.label: Charaeva upsets new World No. 1 Rybakina in Beijing second round
Gauff, Sun set for Beijing battle in junior's first-ever top 5 matchup
By the numbers: Swiatek converts five breaks in China Open opener

content.body:
A day after World No. 1 Elena Rybakina was knocked out of the China Open, World No. 2 Aryna Sabalenka followed suit. Sabalenka was bundled out in the third round in Beijing on Sunday by No. 26 seed Nikola Bartunkova in straight sets, 6-4, 6-3.

Bartunkova, ranked a career-high No. 34 in the world, began the match by breaking Sabalenka’s serve. She saved five break points in a crucial sixth game to maintain her advantage at 4-2. Although she missed three chances in the next game to go up a double break, the Czech held her next two service games to love to close out the first set 6-4.

Bartunkova was the first to break again in the second set to go up 3-1 and did not face a single break point in the set. She broke Sabalenka again in the ninth game to complete the 6-4, 6-3 win in 1 hour, 35 minutes.

She gets it done 🔥

Nikola Bartunkova secures the win of her career defeating No.2 seed Sabalenka in straight sets!#ChinaOpen pic.twitter.com/2NHzzCGrKT

— wta (@WTA) October 4, 2026

Here are some key stats from Bartunkova’s upset win:

0: The number of break points that Sabalenka converted in the match. She earned five break points in the first set and none in the second. Meanwhile, Bartunkova converted three of eight break chances in the match. 

"She is very talented, and moves well on court," Sabalenka said of her opponent after the match. "She also serves well so you have to convert your chances against her. She can serve really well and to return from shade or sun is tricky. I wasn’t good at this today."

2: This is the second time in her career that Bartunkova has reached the round of 16 at a WTA 1000 event. She reached the same stage in Rome, where she lost to eventual champion Elina Svitolina.

"It is the biggest win of my career," Bartunkova said after the match. "It was very difficult conditions for today because half of the court was very cold and very windy. And the other side was very hot and opposite. It was very difficult conditions for both of us. It could be better for sure, especially on my serve. But it was because of the windy and it was cold. So, that's why I think my percentage of my serve was at the low."

2: This was Bartunkova’s second career win over a Top 10 player. Her only previous win came against then No. 10 Belinda Bencic in the second round of this year’s Australian Open. Overall, she is 2-5 against Top 10 players in her career.

3: The number of times Sabalenka has reached the quarterfinals in Beijing - in 2024, when she lost to eventual runner-up Karolina Muchova; in 2023, when she lost to eventual champion Rybakina; and in 2018, when she lost to Wang Qiang. The world No. 2 has now failed to reach the semifinals in all five of her main-draw appearances here.

6: The number of consecutive matches Sabalenka has lost after dropping the first set. Her last win after losing the opening set came against Bartunkova herself in Berlin. Overall, Sabalenka is 3-7 after losing the first set in 2026.

12: The number of years since the top two seeds failed to feature in the round of 16 at the China Open. The last time that happened was in 2015, when No. 1 seed Simona Halep lost to Lara Arruabarrena and No. 2 seed Petra Kvitova lost to Sara Errani.

22: This was 20-year-old Bartunkova’s 22nd win of the season, including her 16th on hard courts, making this her most successful season on tour to date.

"For me, it's an unbelievable year for me," she told the media after the win. "I didn't expect before this year that I would play like this. And I would be here like this. It's great. But just now, I just focus on myself, improve my game. Because still, it's 50-50-50 every match. And I'm still young. I need to have more experience. That's my goal right now."

24: The number of times Sabalenka has faced an opponent ranked outside the Top 20 in 2026. This was her second loss in those 24 matches, with the other coming against Bartunkova’s compatriot Sara Bejlek in the Cincinnati round of 16.

Bartunkova will next face Austria’s Sinja Kraus for a spot in the quarterfinals. Kraus scored a 6-1, 6-4 win over Dayana Yastremska. The Czech holds a 1-0 record against Kraus, having defeated her in Hechingen in 2025.
content.summary: Nikola Bartunkova scored the biggest win of her career by defeating No. 2 seed Aryna Sabalenka in the third round of the China Open on Sunday. The Czech claimed her second career Top 10 victory and advanced to the round of 16 for the second time at a WTA 1000 event.

content.title: Gauff, Sun set for Beijing battle in junior's first-ever top 5 matchup
content.description: World No. 3 Coco Gauff was once a junior with all the attention on her seven years ago. No win 2026, she's set to face the latest junior on the rise in China's Sun Xinran.

related.label: Sun, 16, upsets Bucsa in Beijing; Zheng advances after Kalinskaya retires
Ahead of WTA debut in Beijing, get to know 16-year-old junior No. 1 Sun Xinran
Around Beijing: Ostapenko enters influencer era as Sakkari's mindset evolves

content.body:
BEIJING -- When Coco Gauff burst onto the scene seven years ago, all eyes were on the then 15-year-old. 

At the 2019 Wimbledon Championships, Gauff made her statement run from qualifying to the fourth round, highlighted by a win over her idol Venus Williams in her first-ever Grand Slam main draw match. 

Now, in 2026 at 22 years old, Gauff is well-established with two major titles among her 12 total on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz. Monday in Beijing, Gauff will have the chance to compete against 16-year-old Sun Xinran, the World No. 1 junior player from China who is receiving heightened attention as she's amid her WTA tour-level debut in her home country. Just a few weeks ago, she won the US Open junior title.

"I think she is really promising," Gauff said on Sun to press after her second round win Saturday. "At 16, to be winning a junior slam, being able to compete on the biggest tournament probably so far of her career. I know she's going to play great tennis against me. I've been in that position."

Sun's Beijing campaign has seen her upset Eva Lys 6-1, 3-0 ret. in the first round and Cristina Bucsa 6-4, 7-5 in the second round. 

"I'm really, really happy to have this chance playing Coco Gauff because she's a Grand Slam champion," Sun said to press in Mandarin. "I've been watching her matches on TV. This is a really great opportunity through my own effort. I will value this opportunity. I will try to do my best."

Despite her age, Sun has stacked up well in her early matches. Against Lys on Thursday, she put on a show to begin the night session on Capital Diamond Court, the venue's center court. Naturally, she's been feeling quite nervous before the matches, but once she hits the court, she doesn't think about the difference in experience. 

"Before the match I was pretty nervous," Sun said. "[Bucsa] is of a higher ranking, but I didn't think too much because I was just focusing point by point. When I'm on the court, I think I'm not that bad and there is not such a big gap."

"I do not think too much into it," Sun added. "This is not something surprising because I know my tennis and I trust myself I could do these things. I'm not worse than other players."

Gauff reflected on her first year on the WTA Tour and said that it's the easiest in a way because every matchup is new, opponents don't have prior to experience to compare with and there isn't last year's points to defend. 

"From that age, everything feels so new and fresh," Gauff said. "I don't think even people are going to put pressure on her. They just want to see her win."

She did have some advice for the teenager, and that is to not have too high standards as she transitions to from juniors to the professional level in the coming years.

"I think the biggest advice when you're second year on tour, try not to keep those same expectations," Gauff said. "She'll be 17 on her second year. Remember that you're 17 years old, you're going to fail, you're going to succeed.

"Obviously when you're young, especially coming from juniors when you're used to winning, it's sometimes tough to lose. I think it's really cool for her to continue to have a good tournament."
content.summary: World No. 3 Coco Gauff was once a junior with all the attention on her seven years ago. No win 2026, she's set to face the latest junior on the rise in China's Sun Xinran.

content.title: Charaeva upsets new World No. 1 Rybakina in Beijing second round
content.description: Alina Charaeva stunned newly crowned World No. 1 Elena Rybakina 3-6, 6-4, 6-3 on Saturday night in Beijing. The 24-year-old, playing only her 17th tour-level main-draw match, became the lowest-ranked player to rally from a set down and defeat the World No. 1.

related.label: Sun, 16, upsets Bucsa in Beijing; Zheng advances after Kalinskaya retires
Gauff gets back into 'match mode' with gritty Beijing opening win over Osorio
By the numbers: Swiatek converts five breaks in China Open opener

content.body:
Entering the week, only one player in WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz history had lost her first match as World No. 1. Make it two after No. 118 Alina Charaeva rallied from a set down to upset Elena Rybakina 3-6, 6-4, 6-3 in 2 hours and 11 minutes on Saturday night in Beijing.

Beijing: Scores | Order of play | Draws

Since the rankings were first published in 1975, Charaeva is just the ninth player outside the Top 100 to defeat the World No. 1 and the lowest-ranked player to claim a comeback win against the World No. 1.

"I don't have words honestly, playing Elena and the World No. 1, it's such a good experience," Charaeva said. "I'm really happy to manage my emotions and play my best tennis.

"I was just trying to stay really hard mentally and keep believing that at some point I could turn it around again to my side," Charaeva added on court. "And I guess I just never stopped believing."

BELIEVE IT, ALINA 🔥🔥🔥

Alina Charaeva just took out World No. 1 Elena Rybakina in Beijing.#ChinaOpen pic.twitter.com/R2Ldf6pQxM

— wta (@WTA) October 3, 2026

Playing just her 17th tour-level main-draw match, the 24-year-old far surpassed the best win of her career. Her previous top-ranked victory came against No. 31 Wang Xinyu earlier this year. With the upset, Charaeva advanced to the third round of the China Open, where she will face Sonay Kartal for the first time.

She was extremely nervous coming into the match, but she made sure that she would just enjoy her time on court regardless of the result.

"Of course, I was just trying to enjoy, to not be so nervous. It wasn't possible. I was so nervous anyway," Charaeva said. "I knew if I could bring the best of myself today, I could fight her. So yeah, I'm just really happy that I could manage it."

How it happened

It was a dream start for Charaeva, who broke in the opening game thanks to four unforced errors from Rybakina. But the top seed recovered quickly and immediately earned the break back, beginning a pattern that continued into the second set.

Rybakina broke for 4-2 in the first set, followed by a break for 4-3 from Charaeva. But Rybakina answered with a backhand return winner to take a 5-3 lead, then held to love to clinch the opening set after 44 minutes.

In the second, a forehand winner gave Rybakina an early 2-1 edge before Charaeva broke right back for 2-2 with a forehand winner of her own. A few games later, a pretty backhand passing shot earned her a fourth break and sent the match to a decider.

To a third set we go 🚨

Alina Charaeva takes the second set off of a Rybakina 6-4.#ChinaOpen pic.twitter.com/fdpPpMGLV8

— wta (@WTA) October 3, 2026

Rybakina saved a break point and held for 2-2 in the third, but Charaeva got the break she needed at 4-2 when Rybakina missed a backhand wide. She consolidated with a love hold, and a few games later served out the match to put the finishing touches on the unlikeliest of upsets.

The result left Rybakina joining Naomi Osaka, who lost to Kristina Mladenovic in Dubai in 2019 in her first match as World No. 1, in an undesirable club.

"Obviously it was a very tough day out there," Rybakina said after the match. "There was a lot going on after the US Open victory. I didn't get a lot of chances to sleep and recover. Congratulations to Alina. She played a very good match, and I felt my foot a little bit at the end of the match. So it's time to rest a little bit and see what is next in the upcoming weeks.

"Thank you to all the fans for supporting and see you next year Beijing. Next I will take a week to rest and hopefully get my foot back to 100% so I can compete in the following tournaments to complete the 2026 season."

What it means

The victory leaves Charaeva in uncharted territory. It was her first Top 10 win in her first opportunity and sent her to the third round of a WTA 1000 event for the first time.

“This is just insane!” 😤#ChinaOpen pic.twitter.com/pTYHE9Lhqk

— wta (@WTA) October 3, 2026

"It will be such a new step for me," Charaeva said. "Of course, I will be really happy to stay some more days in Beijing. I really enjoy the fans, the city and the organization."

It also sets the stage for a potential Top 100 debut, a mission that would be aided by a win in her next match. It would be the latest in a string of accomplishments this season for Charaeva, who won her first WTA 125 title in Midland in February and reached her first two tour-level quarterfinals in Hamburg and Sao Paulo.

content.title: Sun, 16, upsets Bucsa in Beijing; Zheng advances after Kalinskaya retires
content.description: Two generations of Chinese tennis scored second-round wins at the China Open on Saturday -- 16-year-old Sun Xinran continued her breakthrough with an upset of Cristina Bucsa, while Zheng Qinwen advanced when Anna Kalinskaya was forced to retire due to illness.

related.label: Gauff gets back into 'match mode' with gritty Beijing opening win over Osorio
Around Beijing: Ostapenko enters influencer era as Sakkari's mindset evolves
By the numbers: Swiatek converts five breaks in China Open opener

content.body:
Representing two generations of Chinese tennis, wild cards Sun Xinran and Zheng Qinwen thrilled the China Open fans on Saturday as they booked their spots in the third round of their home tournament.

Junior World No. 1 Sun stunned No. 27 seed Cristina Bucsa 6-4, 7-5 in 1 hour and 31 minutes to become the first 2010-born player to win a completed match at WTA 1000 level or above. The 16-year-old, fresh off the girls' title at the US Open, is making her WTA main-draw debut this week. She'll next face another player who knows a thing or two about making a mark at a young age -- No. 3 seed Coco Gauff, the 2024 Beijing champion.

Olympic gold medallist Zheng, who put together a memorable run to the US Open quarterfinals as a qualifier, continued her resurgence by advancing when No. 15 seed Anna Kalinskaya was forced to retire due to illness trailing 6-7(4), 6-4, 3-0. She'll next face No. 18 seed Marie Bouzkova for the first time after the Czech player ended Seoul champion Kimberly Birrell's six-match winning streak 6-4, 6-4.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

Sun had already delivered an eye-catching performance in her first round, winning nine straight games in a blaze of winners before Eva Lys retired trailing 6-1, 3-0 due to a foot injury. Against a stronger and healthier opponent in Bucsa, the teenager soon showed she could back up her opening result in a full match.

Indeed, it was Sun's composure in closing it out that was most impressive. After erasing an early 2-0 deficit in the second set, she advanced to a game of victory at 5-4 -- but Bucsa, swarming the net, raised her game to level at 5-5. Momentum threatened to turn the Spaniard's way as she held a break point for 6-5. Sun responded brilliantly, swatting a forehand winner down the line to stave it off. A game later, she sealed victory on her first match point by threading a forehand pass.

"I feel really excited before the match," Sun said afterwards. "I know she is really good player. I just want to play my best tennis. First set start really hard because I was little bit nervous. After I feel better and better. Just like this."

Currently ranked No. 582, Sun is guaranteed to make her Top 500 debut following Beijing. She'll become the third 2010-born player to do so, following Memphis champion Kristina Liutova (currently No. 119) and Jana Kovackova (currently No. 451).

During her US Open run, Zheng attributed her uptick in form to the intense training block in Florida that she underwent after losing in Toronto qualifying to Lanlana Tararudee. That's shown not just in her results, but her scorelines. Seven of her last nine matches have gone to three sets, and she's won six of those.

Against Kalinskaya, Zheng piled on the first-strike pressure early. In a remarkable game at 2-2 in the first set, she fired five aces, eventually tallying 13 overall. But there was also a lack of consistency that meant she was unable to close out a 5-3 lead, with Kalinskaya finding better serves when it matters to snatch the tiebreak.

The Roland Garros quarterfinalist had the opportunity to press home her advantage when she held two break points for 2-0 in the second set, but was unable to take either. Zheng continued to slam a succession of return winners off the Kalinskaya delivery, and was eventually rewarded with the break for 4-3 -- and this time, she made no mistake in closing the set out.

Kalinskaya received a medical timeout after the first game of the decider, and lasted just two more games before pulling the plug.

Though pleased with how she responded in the second set, Zheng wasn't entirely satisfied with her performance.

"I was 5-3 up, then I couldn't get the first set when I had my serve on my hand," she said in her press conference. "I kind of feel like I make the match difficult today 'cause I got lot of break point in the first set ... So takes a while to change a bit the mentality in the second set.

"But I was just happy that I'm able to get the match, even she retired. But I felt like the match is quite on my dynamic."
content.summary: Two generations of Chinese tennis scored second-round wins at the China Open on Saturday -- 16-year-old Sun Xinran continued her breakthrough with an upset of Cristina Bucsa, while Zheng Qinwen advanced when Anna Kalinskaya was forced to retire due to illness.

content.title: Around Beijing: Ostapenko enters influencer era as Sakkari's mindset evolves
content.description: In Beijing, Jelena Ostapenko chatted about her latest endeavor with short-form digital content while Maria Sakkari discussed how her mindset has changed over the course of the 2026 season.

related.label: By the numbers: Swiatek converts five breaks in China Open opener
Gauff gets back into 'match mode' with gritty Beijing opening win over Osorio
Vote: What was the best shot of the week in Beijing?

content.body:
BEIJING -- Jelena Ostapenko is a person of many endeavors. 

Aside from being the World No. 32 on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz, she has her own merchandise line, runs a personal baking Instagram account and now currently is entering her influencer era with an influx of short-form, day-in-the-life content over the past few months to give fans a glimpse behind the scenes. 

In her recent content, she's posted anything from short-form travel videos to a side-quest visiting Niagara Falls and more. 

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Jelena Ostapenko (@jelena.ostapenko)

The decision to post more of the digital content came at the advice of the Grand Slam champion's personal assistant.

"She knows a lot about marketing and those kind of things," Ostapenko said after her second-round China Open win. "A few times, she was trying to tell me that probably I needed to have more active social media."

Ostapenko was initially hesitant on the idea, but suddenly, she just went for it one day.

"I was like, 'No, I don't want it, I don't want it.' Then at some point, I was like, 'OK, let's see how it goes,' Ostapenko said. "It's going pretty well, especially TikTok. I have some videos [with] over 300,000 views, which is pretty good. I'm looking forward now to posting some more nice things, and I think for fans, it's kind of interesting to see what's happening."

In Beijing, Ostapenko is through to the third round and will face Elise Mertens on Monday. Saturday, she defeated Paula Badosa in a close 7-6(5), 7-5 win to earn her fourth win over the Spaniard.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Jelena Ostapenko (@jelena.ostapenko)

Though the summer didn't see the results in singles, coming to China was something Ostapenko looked forward to, even saying that it feels like a "second home" and enjoys receiving several customized gifts from the fans.

"It's been a while in singles, and I'm really happy to be in China," Ostapenko said. "The Chinese fans are super special for me, and today I felt an amazing atmosphere. I felt I'm playing in my second home. So many people supporting me, and I had so many nice gifts. Every gift is like super special, so I really love to come here."

Sakkari has moved on from chasing points 'obsession'

Nine months ago at the United Cup in Perth, Maria Sakkari spoke confidently in her ability about gradually getting back to where she once was -- in the top 10. In western Australia, she was ranked No. 51 and has slowly made her way to No. 33 and is the No. 25 seed in Beijing. 

An objective for 2026 was that she wasn't going to chase points, and be more strategic of the tournaments she plays. As the season has evolved, that "get back to the top" mindset has also evolved. While she recognizes improving her ranking is important, she isn't living her life on tour constantly thinking about the number.

"I think that in the beginning of the year, I had this obsession about getting back to the top," Sakkari said to wtatennis.com after her 6-2, 6-2 win over Storm Hunter. "I feel I've done really well just not thinking about it. It's kind of irrelevant right now, and just try, play and enjoy as much as I can." 

Still, Sakkari recognizes the ranking is important for direct entry into top tournaments, possible seeding implications and avoiding top ranked players in early rounds. 

"The ranking is important and relevant, but at the same time, I feel like the obsession that I had being one of the best is gone, which is very good," Sakkari added. "I'm enjoying a lot more being on the tour like that, and I just proud of who I am."

Sakkari always enjoys the Asian Swing and the cities that she visits. While there isn't a Grand Slam at the end of this stretch, she's never really viewed previous tournaments in other swings as if she were preparing for a major. 

"I never played the lead-up tournaments thinking that it's a Slam coming up," Sakkari said. "I feel a lot of players are tired during this [swing] so I feel it's a good challenge to push and just play some good matches, make some points and and finish the year strong.

"Whoever handles this trip better, plays better. Obviously, everyone's fatigued. Everyone's has playing too much, traveled a lot, but I feel it's a good chance to just push yourself, try and do as good as possible."

Sakkari will next face No. 6 seed Elina Svitolina, who defeated Katerina Siniakova in three sets.

content.description: Former champion Iga Swiatek began her China Open campaign with a straight-sets victory over Chinese wild card Xinyu Gao in Beijing on Saturday. The No. 8 seed converted five of eight break points and recorded her 146th career WTA 1000 main-draw match win.

By the numbers: Sabalenka overwhelms Zarazua with 36 winners in Beijing opener
Maja Chwalinska’s feather-light finish earns September Shot of the Month

content.body:
Former champion and No. 8 seed Iga Swiatek opened her campaign for a second China Open title with a straight-sets win over local wild card Xinyu Gao in the second round in Beijing on Saturday.

Swiatek, who won the title here in 2023, exchanged an early break of serve with the 244th-ranked Chinese player before gaining a two-break advantage to claim the first set 6-2. The Polish star, ranked No. 9, broke twice again in the second set to close out a 6-2, 6-3 win in 1 hour, 27 minutes.

What a way to finish!@iga_swiatek secures the win to move on into the third round in Beijing.#ChinaOpen pic.twitter.com/pSxfmpXg95

— wta (@WTA) October 3, 2026

"For sure, it was a solid match," Swiatek said after her win. "Many long rallies. I'm happy about that because I had a chance to get the rhythm of the court, feel the ball. For sure a good start. I'm happy to be back here."

Here are some key numbers from Swiatek's latest win:

5: The number of break points Swiatek converted in the match from eight opportunities. Gao earned only one break point and converted it.

6: This was Swiatek's sixth opening-match win in seven WTA 1000 events this season. Her only opening-round loss at a WTA 1000 event this year came in Miami, where she fell to compatriot Magda Linette.

6: This was Swiatek's sixth win in seven matches against opponents ranked outside the Top 100. Her only loss came to No. 121-ranked Zheng Qinwen in the fourth round of the US Open.

9: Swiatek has captured nine wins from her first 10 matches at this tournament. That is the most of any player, tying her with Coco Gauff and Svetlana Kuznetsova. 

146: This was Swiatek's 146th career main-draw match win at WTA 1000-level events. Only two currently active players have more career main-draw match-wins at the WTA 1000 level -- Aryna Sabalenka (156) and Serena Williams (148).

4: Swiatek holds a 4-0 record against her next opponent, No. 30 seed Donna Vekic. Vekic defeated another Chinese wild card, Lin Zhu, 6-4, 6-2 to book her place in the third round. Three of Swiatek's four wins over Vekic have come in straight sets. This will be their fourth meeting on hard courts. 

Swiatek added that qualifying for the season-ending WTA Finals remains a big goal for her in the coming weeks

"For sure that's the goal. I'm going to be fighting for that. Obviously I'm aware. But it doesn't change the fact that it still feels pretty far as there are many tournaments where you can gain many points.

"I try to just take it step by step because if I'm focused only on the next match, this is where I perform my best. I've never been in this position, so for sure it's another experience in my career."

content.title: Gauff gets back into 'match mode' with gritty Beijing opening win over Osorio
content.description: Coco Gauff's streak of reaching at least semifinals was in jeopardy Saturday, but the 2024 Beijing champion's third-set push solidified a gritty win over Camila Osorio in her first match back since the US Open.

related.label: Vote: What was the best shot of the week in Beijing?
By the numbers: Sabalenka overwhelms Zarazua with 36 winners in Beijing opener
Around Beijing's grounds: Preston highlights upset-filled day, Czechs dominate

content.body:
BEIJING -- Coco Gauff's three-year streak of reaching at least the semifinals of the China Open was put to test Saturday, but with a 7-6(4), 4-6, 6-2 gritty win over Camila Osorio, the 2024 Beijing champ is through to the third round.

It wasn't easy as Osorio broke Gauff's serve five times and won just four less total points than the American. There were multiple times Gauff was visibly upset with her performance, even during the first set which she had won, particularly when Gauff had a 5-2 first set lead be dwindled into the tiebreak. 

In three previous Beijing opening matches, Gauff had won all in straight sets, and after a stressful test, Gauff will face the winner of Cristina Bucsa and Chinese junior No. 1 Sun Xinran. She has now won seven of eight opening WTA 1000 matches this season with the lone defeat coming to Elisabetta Cocciaretto in Doha. 

"I think just the reset in the third," Gauff said to press on what she was most pleased with Saturday. "Honestly, I don't know, there was a moment in the match I got really frustrated. I feel Camila is that type of player [who] can really frustrate you. I was able to rest for the third set, so just to be able to forget about the second set."

Gauff played her first match back since a semifinal run at the US Open, and Saturday was the first time she played Osorio on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz. As it was her first match in nearly three weeks, Gauff was focused on getting back into "match mode," and felt that it was a good transition into the final part of the season despite the uneasiness.  

"I think this time of the year, it's really a final push and I think today was a good match to start of the Asian Swing." 

GAUFF GOES THROUGH 🔥@CocoGauff takes the win in a hard fought match against Osorio to continue her run in Beijing!#ChinaOpen pic.twitter.com/yt0a6dYMhu

— wta (@WTA) October 3, 2026

Furthermore, China has been one of Gauff's hottest stops on the WTA Tour. Her win marked Gauff's 23rd win at a WTA event in China, and her 88.4% win rate (23-3 record) in China is the best of any player this century (minimum 10 matches). In addition to Beijing two years ago, Gauff won Wuhan in 2025.

Ahead of the tournament, Gauff said she feels a bit more relaxed this time of year, and that there's "a lot less chaos" with the Grand Slams being complete. 

"I just go into this swing always just trying to push," Gauff said. "This is the final push for the Finals, the final push of the year. Every match counts. Every match counts throughout the season, but even more so now I feel like.

"I think knowing that I have good results here in China maybe allows me to be more confident, especially when the matches get tough."
content.author: Cole Bambini

content.title: Vote: What was the best shot of the week in Beijing?
content.description: We've combed through the early-round matches in Beijing and picked our top five shots. Check them out, and make sure to vote for your favorite at the bottom.

By the numbers: Sabalenka overwhelms Zarazua with 36 winners in Beijing opener
Anatomy of a hot shot: Karolina Muchova on her 360-degree spin in Beijing

content.body:
It was a short week, with the China Open in Beijing not getting underway until Wednesday. But with a stacked 96-player draw, there was no shortage of matches -- and no shortage of incredible shots.

We've combed through the early rounds in Beijing and picked our five favorite shots. Which do you think was the best? Check them out below, and vote for your WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz shot of the week at the bottom.

Sara Bejlek's running forehand crosscourt lob

Sara Bejlek was a human highlight reel in her Beijing debut. Leading 4-2 in the first set, she hit a running forehand crosscourt lob that landed just inside the baseline. 

Then in the first point of the second set, after a lengthy rally, she hit a drop shot to force Maddison Inglis in. After Inglis dumped it back over the net, Bejlek put her away with the forehand winner.

Bejlek won the match 6-3, 7-5.

Karolina Muchova's 360-degree pickup and pass

Karolina Muchova routinely pulls off shots that we've never seen before. She did it again on Friday, against Katie Boulter.

At 3-all in the first-set tiebreaker, Boulter returned Muchova's serve just beyond the baseline. The Wimbledon runner-up responded with an improbable 360-degree spinning pickup. Boulter got to it and beautifully flicked it toward the sideline. Muchova read it, shuffled to the alley and won the point with a perfectly-angled pass.

Muchova won the tiebreaker and rolled in the second set for the 7-6 (3), 6-1 win.

Linda Noskova's pinpoint lobs

While we're on the subject of Czech shot-makers, Linda Noskova showed off pinpoint precision against Elena-Gabriela Ruse. At 2-0, 15-all in the first set, Noskova hit a drop shot to bring Ruse in, then hit a lob on the short hop that sailed over her head and landed just in front of the line. 

Later in the set, with Noskova leading 3-0, she hit a running forehand lob that floated just past Ruse's outstretched racquet.

Noskova went on to win 6-4, 6-1.

Ekaterina Alexandrova's forehand flicks at full stretch

Ekaterina Alexandrova had the touch on Friday against Aliaksandra Sasnovich.

In the first game of the match, on ad point, Alexandrova flicked a crosscourt winner that snuck over the net. Later in the set, at 4-0, 30-15, she pulled it off again, a mirror image of the first winner.

Alexandrova won 6-1, 6-4.

Sun Xinran's drop shot winner

Sun Xinran wasted little time showing fans why she's the junior World No. 1.

Leading Eva Lys 2-1 in the first set in her WTA debut, Sun ended a punishing 22-stroke rally with a drop shot winner, pulling the string after repeated blows from the baseline.

Three games later, the power was back on display. The US Open junior champion ended an even longer rally -- this one 23 shots -- with a backhand winner into the corner.

The 16-year-old was leading Lys 6-1, 3-0 when Lys retired with a foot injury.
content.author: Brad Kallet

content.title: Anatomy of a hot shot: Karolina Muchova on her 360-degree spin in Beijing
content.description: Karolina Muchova came up with an absurd piece of athletic artistry (again) in the China Open second round. But have these hot shots become so commonplace for the Czech that she now finds them routine and unmemorable?

related.label: Former champ Osaka survives stern test from Timofeeva in Beijing
Andreeva and Noskova advance in Beijing with bigger goals in sight
Maja Chwalinska’s feather-light finish earns September Shot of the Month

content.body:
Is it possible to play so many hot shots that they become routine -- unmemorable, even?

Apparently so for Karolina Muchova. With her second-round match against Katie Boulter at the China Open poised at 3-3 in the first-set tiebreak, the Czech came up with some dizzying wizardry -- a full 360-degree spinning pickup, then a finely angled pass at full stretch past the flailing Briton.

It wasn't just a sensational piece of athletic artistry, but the key point of the match. It effectively ended Boulter's impact on the contest -- Muchova did not drop another point in the tiebreak, then ran away with the second set for a 7-6(3), 6-1 victory. Most players would be dining out on it for weeks, if not years, to come.

But asked about it afterwards, the two-time major finalist had no idea what reporters were talking about. "My spin shot?" she asked, quizzically. She had to be shown a clip of it to jog her memory.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

Once Muchova was watching it back, though, she was able to explain how she pulled it off -- as much as one can explain genius in mere human language, at any rate.

"[I feel I'm] quite well under, like on my feet," she recalled. "I feel like this was the only way to kind of pick it up. It went naturally because I had it behind my body, so my body went that way. It's not that I was thinking about it ahead. I would rather hit nice easy backhand volley, but this was out of it. I'm happy that I managed to win that shot."

It's simple -- and maybe even forgettable -- when you put it like that. But most importantly, there'll be the chance to see what else Muchova can come up with in Beijing: the No. 7 seed has advanced to face No. 29 seed Liudmila Samsonova in the third round.
content.author: Alex Macpherson
content.summary: Karolina Muchova came up with an absurd piece of athletic artistry (again) in the China Open second round. But have these hot shots become so commonplace for the Czech that she now finds them routine and unmemorable?

content.title: By the numbers: Sabalenka overwhelms Zarazua with 36 winners in Beijing opener
content.description: Aryna Sabalenka returned to the court on Friday, defeating Renata Zarazua 6-1, 6-3 in 62 minutes to reach the third round in Beijing. The World No. 2 struck 36 winners, fired 11 aces and never faced a break point as she improved to 2-0 against Zarazua.

related.label: Former champ Osaka survives stern test from Timofeeva in Beijing
Andreeva and Noskova advance in Beijing with bigger goals in sight
Around Beijing's grounds: Preston highlights upset-filled day, Czechs dominate

content.body:
Playing her first match since the US Open final, Aryna Sabalenka delivered a statement performance in her Beijing opener Friday, defeating Renata Zarazua 6-1, 6-3 in 62 minutes to reach the third round.

Beijing: Scores | Order of play | Draws

In a victory that saw the World No. 2 finish with 36 winners, two more than Zarazua's total points won (34), Sabalenka had plenty to like about her effort.

"I'm definitely happy with the level I played at," Sabalenka told reporters. "Not much to complain about. Happy with the focus, happy physically and with the performance. Happy to be through."

Closing out Day 3 in style ✨@SabalenkaA defeats Zarazua in Beijing!#ChinaOpen pic.twitter.com/DWmTVbLY1Y

— wta (@WTA) October 2, 2026

Sabalenka improved to 2-0 against Zarazua at the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz level. Notably, the last time she defeated Zarazua, in Brisbane last year, she went on to win the tournament. That could be an encouraging sign for Sabalenka, who has reached the quarterfinals in Beijing three times but never advanced further.

There is still plenty of tennis left to be played, but the early returns were promising.

Sabalenka raced to a fast start, breaking for 2-0 with a forehand return winner before breaking again for 5-1 with another forehand return winner. A backhand winner gave her set point, and she followed with a forehand passing shot to close out the opening set in 31 minutes.

In control in the first 💪@SabalenkaA takes a 6-1 lead against Zarazua!#ChinaOpen pic.twitter.com/pzgy1z3Q2W

— wta (@WTA) October 2, 2026

After Zarazua held serve to begin the second, Sabalenka won the next 12 points for a 3-1 lead. Zarazua stayed within striking distance, but Sabalenka produced a love hold featuring four winners, including three aces, in the penultimate game before breaking serve one final time to complete the straight-sets victory.

Here are the numbers to know following Sabalenka's return to the court.

3: First-serve points lost. Sabalenka won 22 of 25 first-serve points, an 88% success rate. She also won 10 of 14 second-serve points (71%).

11: Aces. The former World No. 1 delivered a dominant all-around serving performance, recording 11 aces and not facing a single break point.

82.7: Win rate in China. Sabalenka improved to 43-9 record at WTA events in China, excluding team competitions. Only Coco Gauff (88.0%), Serena Williams (83.3%) and Iga Swiatek (83.3%) own higher winning percentages.

83.9: Winning percentage in 2026. Sabalenka has the highest win rate on tour this season with her 47-9 record. Karolina Muchova is second at 40-10 (80.0%).

99: Winners-to-unforced errors differential at WTA 1000s. After finishing plus-22 on Friday, Sabalenka owns the best differential on tour this season. Clara Tauson is next at plus-22.

What's next

Sabalenka will face No. 26 seed Nikola Bartunkova in the third round after the young Czech defeated Magdalena Frech 6-2, 6-2 on Friday. Sabalenka won their only previous meeting, rallying from 6-2, 4-0 down in the Berlin quarterfinals earlier this season.
